correctness.rationale: The frozen proof asserts an incorrect exact backward equation (RESULT.md lines 56–60), rather than an incorrect threshold. Let u,r be respectively the half-sum and half-difference of the first moments, and m,h those of the second moments. With f=−1/(1+x), the generator equations give f u′+v r′=−1, f m′+v h′=−2u, and v m′+f h′−2γh=−2r. Thus 2γv h=(v²−f²)m′−2fu+2vr. Differentiate and substitute for r′ and h′: (v²−f²)m″+2f(γ−f′)m′=2(f′−2γ)u+4fu′+2, not +4. Independent symbolic elimination confirms this; the frozen checker only asserts the two Lyapunov identities and leading coefficient matching, so it does not detect the error. The incorrect constant does not affect leading-order conclusions. The protected interval is invariant, with uniformly positive absorption probability in fixed time blocks at the turning point. In the exterior, finite moments propagate between signs and launch points by positive-probability deterministic-direction runs and flips; on a compact interior interval, no-flip probabilities from its endpoints bound the moments uniformly, and conditioning at the next flip or downstream endpoint gives the classical backward equations since neither drift vanishes there. The Lyapunov calculations reproduce exactly: H_2=y²+(v/γ)σy has generator −2(1−D)−vσ/(γy), and H_4=y⁴+(2v/γ)σy³ has generator −4(1−3D)y²−6vσy/γ, y=1+x. For D<1/3 a positive combination, shifted to be nonnegative, controls the integral of twice the first moment up to hitting the turning point; the protected-region remainder is uniformly bounded. This gives the O(x⁴) bound needed to remove the homogeneous solution. In the corrected equation, the integrating factor is proportional to x^(−1/D), and the divided forcing still has leading term −2c x²/D, c=1/[2(1−D)]. For 1/3<D<1 integrating gives m′∼−2c x³/(3D−1); at D=1/3 it gives m′∼−6c x³ log x, contradicting a nonnegative m in both regimes. At D≥1 mean divergence suffices. For D<1/3 integration from infinity gives m′∼2c x³/(1−3D); the displayed exact relation for h gives h=O(x³), preserving the coefficient in each sign. Thus the theorem is supported after correcting the false identity, not refuted. The fixed-mesh killed-box experiments at lower level 1.5 (the turning point is 1 for v=0.5) can corroborate cutoff trends only; they do not verify the critical logarithm or identify infinite-domain moments. No replacement was submitted because the corrected scientific claim is independently covered by the catalogue comparisons below.
